metadata.title: How to Make a Flavorful Italian Dressing
metadata.description: Learn how to make a flavorful Italian dressing with Chef Mark from LearnToCook.com. For a complete recipe to accompany this video please visit http://learntocook.com/salad/how-to-make-a-flavorful-italian-dressing/

nodes.plm_action: Process them together until the mixture is smooth and consistent.
nodes.plm_caption:
A chef is seen in the kitchen preparing a dish by blending the ingredients in a blender. The chef begins by filling up a blender with various ingredients from a counter and then blends them all together until smooth. Finally, the chef takes the contents out of the blender and pours into a small bowl.
There are various objects in the kitchen, including a refrigerator and ovens. The kitchen is dimly lit while the blender is on. The camera is very close to the blender, and the lighting from inside of it is bright and green. At the end of the video, a logo can be seen with the words "Escoffier School of Culinary Arts." The video is taken during the day, and the lighting is natural.

summary.brief: Chef Mark makes a homemade Italian dressing by mixing vinegar, seasonings and olive oil in a food processor and then pours it into a bowl.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a brief montage that shows a chef slicing vegetables on a cutting board and several short promotional graphics. The scene then cuts to Chef Mark standing at a kitchen counter beside a food processor. He adds white‑wine vinegar, a pinch of sugar, freshly squeezed lemon juice, garlic salt, onion salt, ground black pepper, and a blend of dried Italian herbs (parsley, basil, oregano and additional basil) into the processor. He pulses briefly, then streams olive oil in a steady stream while the processor runs, creating an emulsion. After a final pulse he opens the lid, scoops the smooth Italian dressing out of the processor, and pours it into a small serving bowl, indicating that the dressing is ready to use.

action.detailed: Blend the vinegar, sugar, lemon juice, garlic salt, onion salt, black pepper, dried herbs, and olive oil together in the food processor, then pour the finished dressing into a bowl.
action.actor: Chef Mark, a chef wearing a white coat and apron

summary.brief: Chef Mark mixes a homemade Italian dressing in a food processor.

summary.brief: Chef prepares a homemade Italian dressing using a food processor.
summary.detailed: The video opens with the chef in a white coat standing at a clean countertop with a food processor centered in front of him. He first measures white‑wine vinegar into a small cup and pours it into the processor, then adds a spoonful of sugar, freshly squeezed lemon juice, garlic salt, onion salt, ground black pepper, and a blend of dried Italian herbs (parsley, basil, oregano). After the lid is secured, he pulses the mixture briefly and streams olive oil into the processor while it runs, allowing the oil to emulsify with the other ingredients. He continues pulsing until a smooth dressing forms, then briefly adds a pat of butter and a little more liquid from a bottle while the processor is still running. Near the end he adds a final amount of white powdered seasoning, gives the processor a few more short pulses, and finally pours the finished Italian dressing into a serving bowl.

action.detailed: Add vinegar, sugar, lemon juice, garlic salt, onion salt, pepper, dried herbs, and butter to the food processor, stream olive oil in while pulsing, then blend until smooth and pour into a bowl.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
